label: Сухой / Мокрый
description: Сухой vs мокрый: dry/wet contrasts across genders and everyday scenes.

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Masculine nominative agreement. 'Сухой' takes the masculine ending to match 'воздух'. The weather phrase anchors the form in a daily observation.
Strategic focus: Feminine nominative agreement. 'Мокрая' takes the feminine ending to match 'трава'. The rainy scene roots the form in a familiar outdoor moment.
Strategic focus: Neuter nominative agreement. 'Сухое' takes the neuter ending to match 'полотенце'. The household detail makes the neuter form concrete.
Strategic focus: Plural nominative agreement. 'Мокрые' takes the plural ending to match 'ботинки'. The everyday complaint fixes the plural form in mind.

missions.phrase: Возьми сухое полотенце, а мокрое повесь.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Direct neuter contrast. 'Сухое' and 'мокрое' both match the neuter 'полотенце', whose accusative equals the nominative. The instruction pairs both adjectives in one action.
Strategic focus: Plural accusative agreement. 'Сухие' matches the inanimate plural 'носки', whose accusative equals the nominative. The short command keeps the form practical.
Strategic focus: Feminine instrumental in the predicate. After past-tense 'была', 'мокрой' takes the feminine instrumental ending to match 'дорога'. This shows the быть-plus-instrumental pattern.
Strategic focus: Plural instrumental in the predicate. After 'были', 'сухими' takes the plural instrumental ending to match 'дрова'. The sentence extends the pattern into the plural.

missions.phrase: Зонт промок, а плащ ещё сух.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Short-form masculine predicate. The short form 'сух' states a present quality of 'плащ' without an ending. Short forms are typical when describing a current state.
Strategic focus: Comparative form. 'Суше' is the comparative of 'сухой' and stays the same for any gender. The sentence compares today's weather to yesterday's.
